newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yugoslav opposition may boycott presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav opposition may boycott presidential poll.

text.p: A Serbian opposition leader said on Saturday his allied parties would boycott presidential elections this year unless President Slobodan Milosevic met their demands to recognise opposition poll victories.

Zoran Djindjic told German regional Hesse Radio that a government admission on Friday that the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition won municipal elections in four cities including Belgrade last November was not enough, and that Zajedno had proof it had won in 14 cities.

Djindjic, leader of the opposition Democratic Party, said the opposition was prepared to talk to Milosevic, but only n condition that he end state censorship of the media to allow free reporting of the protests.
If the president did not show he was ready to make concessions, Zajedno would not only boycott the presidential elections but also withdraw its members from parliament.

Serbian presidential elections are due by the end of the year. After a landslide victory last November for the federal parliament, the ruling socialists hinted that Milosevic would hold them as early as in March to capitalise on his popularity.

But the defeat at the local elections and ensuing mass protests that have gone on daily for several weeks have delayed the polls until the end of the year to give Milosevic time to contain the damage, analysts say.
Djindjic said the opposition's goal was to oust Milosevic in democratic elections, but if the president did not alow suitable dmocratic conditions to be created, his overthrow would be inevitable.
